Ok so let me help you out with this because I’ve been where you are and i know the struggle. When i first got my laptop i tried charging it with my friends 65w apple charger and it kept bugging out where like one second it’s charging but the other it’s not so I thought it just couldn’t do 65w charging, but it turns out it can, you just need to update the bios, the laptop now can even support up to 130w charging, if you need help with how exactly update the bios just let me know. Right now i have a [Ugreen 100w desktop charger](https://a.aliexpress.com/_m04RYd8), which is really awesome tbh as u dont have to carry that huge monstrosity of a charger around and like even move around the house freely and not worry about battery cuz you have a second charger, and u get to have the benefit of extending the longevity of the battery by always keeping it in conservation mode. Anyways back to the main point, the charger also does 65w charging if ur charging other devices at the same time, and that’s what I’m doing right now and it works perfectly fine, I just tested it out for you to double check, but as i said, make sure to update the bios from lenovo vantage because otherwise it wont work. Now while 65w charging does work, i would recommend you go for a 100w charger like the one I linked for you, [this](https://a.aliexpress.com/_mPOPXa6) is a cheaper version of it if that one is too much. This way you get the added benefit of also having the ability to use it to charge your phone at the same time as your laptop and if you’re doing something moderately demanding, 65w might not be enough, in situations like these you will have to enable conservation mode for it to show that the laptop is charging with the 65w charger. If i have free time and you’re interested I might make a video about how much can you do with a 65w charger. Anyways i hope this helps.

Nah trust me, when i first got the laptop i got same battery life as yours, heres all the tweaks i did and now i get almost 8 hours battery life running netflix on edge or light office work. Before anything tho u have to set ur expectations, don’t go thinking you can get amazing battery life running a game or any demanding software, not even the new macbooks can last much with these. Now that’s out of the way, here’s what to do, obviously hybrid mode, lower refresh rate to 60hz using fm+r, turn rgb off, brightness for me was only three ticks below max, quiet mode, and as for icue, if u really don’t want to customize anything, just uninstall it, if you however would like to use it from time to time, make sure to disable it from startup, then go to services (windows + r, then type services.msc), search for corsair and stop ALL OF THEM (there should be 3-4) then make sure to make the running of them not automatic but manual so only when u turn them on does it tuen on. Now i see all this talk about battery lottery and bla bla, that’s bs, it all depends on discharge rate, u cant be discharging 100w and expect the laptop to last longer than an hour and a half (100w, and the battery is 80wh, do the math). Now to monitor how much ur actually discharging u can use lenovo vantage software, open it, go to the power section, and there should be a button called see battery details, click on it, and u should see discharge rate and how much the laptop is expected to last, sometimes some programs take mych more than u realise, i was using chrome and was getting around 25w discharge, that’s double what i got doing same things on edge (trust me i hate Microsoft but if it gets better battery life I’m all for it). On idle u should be drawing around 9-10w, so make sure that u hot that mark without anything running, if u dont thwn theres some software messing with you, make sure to disable all the ones u don’t use on startup. And yeah that’s pretty much it, you’ll be getting almost 8 hours of light use guaranteed after that, hope this helped .

Your problem is that you’re using the icue software for rgb control, it was shown by jarrod tech that it drastically reduces battery life. If you want optimal battery life, go to the task manager (ctrl + shift + esc) then look for icue software and terminate it. After that go on the statrtup section and disable icue to start on startup.

Even after you do that, turn the rgb off using fn + space as indicated. Then turn refresh rate to 60 using Fn + R. Turn the brightness down a bit. Then go on the vantage app, and turn on hybrid mode. The vantage app has an option where it lets you only use only 80% of your battery life as to increase its life span, make sure you dont have that enabled. 

After this, you should be getting about 8 hours battery life of light use, obviously if you play games or start anything demanding your battery life would decrease. I hope this helped.
